advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'recorded on EVERY review' claim with the drift_refresh/reuse early-returns that skip record_metrics (either record earlier or narrow the docstring).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:586: `if refreshed is not None:` ... `return findings.validate_structured(refreshed, "plan_review_verdict")` returns before line 742
cited_anchor.py:172 docstring: 'It is written on EVERY review — ``False`` is a measurement, not an absence, and only a recorded ``False`` makes the warning's precision computable.'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:742: `cited_anchor.record_metrics(verdict, anchor_precheck)` is the only call site and sits after all short-circuit returns
advisory.finding: record_metrics is only invoked on the full-review path (line 742), after the drift_refresh early-return at lines 586-589 and after the idempotent_reuse/verdict_reuse short-circuits — so the 'recorded on EVERY review' / 'False is a measurement, not an absence' guarantee that makes offline precision computable is not actually met for those short-circuit cohorts.
scenarios: A ticket resolved via drift_refresh never stamps metrics.precheck.cited_anchor_warning, biasing the offline precision denominator.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Match anchors against the same canonical_description form the component fingerprint hashes (or correct the byte-identical soundness claim in the docstring).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py:127: `"description": canonical_description(ctx.description, normalize_checkboxes=normalize_checkboxes, normalize_whitespace=normalize_whitespace)` — the fingerprinted form is canonicalized, not raw
cited_anchor.py:54 docstring: 'so the plan text itself is byte-identical' — true only for the canonical form, not the raw text the anchor is matched against
advisory.finding: The anchor haystack is the raw description (`_normalize(ctx.description)`), but condition 2 gates on the *canonicalized* description-component fingerprint (canonical_description applies checkbox + insignificant-whitespace normalization). A checkbox flip or insignificant-whitespace edit leaves the component digest unchanged while the raw prose has actually moved, so the docstring's 'the plan text itself is byte-identical' soundness claim is overstated.
scenarios: A blocking finding quotes text near a checkbox that was toggled; the description digest is unchanged (checkbox normalized away) but the raw prose the anchor matches against differs, or vice versa.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test feeding a blocking finding a dict-shaped evidence item ({'quote': ANCHOR}) and a non-string item, asserting the anchor is extracted (warning fires) and the odd item is skipped without raising.
evidence: cited_anchor.py:61-79 `_anchor_texts` handles `isinstance(item, dict)` with `raw = item.get("quote") or item.get("text") or item.get("evidence") or ""` and non-str/non-dict items are `continue`d
cited_anchor.py docstring: 'a mapping carrying a ``quote``/``text``/``evidence`` key is accepted too so a future finder shape degrades to "no anchors" instead of raising'
All test evidence values are list[str]: `"evidence": [ANCHOR]` in _blocking_finding and parametrized cases `([], ["AC 1"], ["a paraphrase..."])`; no dict-item or non-str-item case is exercised
ABSENCE: a regression that broke dict-key extraction, changed the key precedence, or made a non-string item raise instead of being skipped would pass the entire current suite
advisory.finding: The dict-shaped evidence-item branch in _anchor_texts (extracting from mapping items via 'quote'/'text'/'evidence' keys, documented to 'degrade to no anchors instead of raising') is introduced by this change but has no test — every finding in the tests supplies evidence as a list of plain strings.
